Run 6 read it as a city hall; after the redraw I read it at every size as a PARLIAMENT: 'Parliament Building of Quebec (Hôtel du Parlement), Quebec City - tentative' (full 0.35, w300 0.35, w140 0.45), hedged 'could be another Second Empire legislature or city hall'. The note names 'a parliament' as a FAIL, and I gave the college exactly the answer I gave hotel-du-parlement. The scorer also fails it (no accepted phrase in the answer) and the audit records the forbidden reading. The drawing itself is faithful: against rmc-mackenzie-building-elevation-2007.jpg every mustBeRight feature is present (five bays each side, two storeys over a basement row, louvred belfry, segmental hood, green pavilion mansards with oculi and cresting, the flat-topped dark slate tower roof with its round face and lunettes), and nothing on neverAdd is drawn. The redraw moved the reading from civic hall to seat of government but not to college or institution. My reading is that a grey Second Empire facade with a central clock tower and mansard end pavilions reads as government in this game whatever its window heads, because hotel-du-parlement is the same silhouette. That is for the contract owner: the note forbids every marker that would say 'college' (cadets, crest, flag, gate arch). Another redraw may not fix it; deciding what this subject can be asked for may.

findingsForArt.subject: fort-henry, kingston-city-hall, kingston-mills, kingston-lakeshore
findingsForArt.finding: fort-henry (renamed to a landmark, drawing unchanged): 'Fort Henry casemates, Kingston (stone fort with arched casemates and cannons)' at every size (0.45-0.5). No arcade, viaduct, market-hall or prison reading. The gravel parade is still a thin band barely separate from the wall base; present to its detail. kingston-city-hall: named at every size (0.5-0.55); no capitol, courthouse or church reading. kingston-mills: 'canal lock station with lockmaster's house (likely a Rideau Canal lock)' at every size; no dam or weir reading, and it did not merge with the winter canal-lock. kingston-lakeshore: 'waterfront park promenade with sailboats'; no city named from the tiles.

findingsForArt.subject: container-car, player, ranch-barn
findingsForArt.finding: These three fail on wording, and I record them as that rather than overriding the scorer. container-car: 'Railway flatcar carrying stacked shipping containers'. 'flatcar' is one token, so no accepted phrase matched; the thing named is right. One caveat for art: I read a FLAT car, not a well car. The dropped well is drawn, since the car ends stand above the lower box's base, but it did not register. player: the child figure passed ('Child character in winter clothes'), but the elderly bare-headed figure was answered 'Elderly person character in winter coat', which names only a coat. The toque, scarf and mitts were in my cues, not my answer. ranch-barn: 'Red barn / horse stable with a horse behind a rail fence' names every drawn part; the list has 'a horse in a fenced yard beside a barn' but not this wording. See contractDefectsForTheOwner.

findingsForArt.subject: northern-river-bar, granite-erratic
findingsForArt.finding: I agree with both fails. northern-river-bar: 'Riverbank terrain strip: river with grassy far bank and rocky near shore with shrubs' (0.35). At full size I read the black-spruce wall as TALL GRASS and the driftwood as flat stones, and named no forest, no bar and nothing northern. All five features are drawn; the spruce wall is the one that does not read, since its spires are too dense and too short against the top edge to separate into trees. granite-erratic: 'Bare granite rock OUTCROP with a small pond' (0.45). The masses read as bedrock rising from the pavement rather than loose boulders resting on it, even with the contact shadow; 'tide pool' read as a pond. No cairn, marker or monument reading.

findingsForArt.subject: terrace-kiosk
findingsForArt.finding: Led with 'Park bandstand/gazebo' but hedged 'or carousel pavilion' at every size (0.35), as runs 5 and 6 did. 'A carousel' is a named FAIL reading. findingsForArt.subject: city-wall
findingsForArt.finding: Read as 'old stone/brick fortification wall section' (0.3). The returning face is drawn in limestone-shade #8a6256, which read to me as red brick. It is not the brick ramp, so neverAdd 'brick' is not present, but the shade tone of `limestone` is close enough to brick to put the word in a blind answer, and brick is what separates chateau-frontenac from this subject.

findingsForArt.subject: martello-tower
findingsForArt.finding: 'Martello tower with wooden upper storey' at every size (0.35-0.4), with no lighthouse, silo or blockhouse reading. The place guess was wrong (Kingston's Murney Tower rather than Tower 1, Québec), pushed by the Kingston prime. The place is accepted, not required.
